issues.body: `approval_probe_order()` exempts only `MAINTAINER_LOGIN` and `APP_BOT_LOGIN`; every other write/maintain/admin collaborator remains in `rest[:APPROVAL_REACTOR_PROBE_CAP]`. An attacker can add 50 lexicographically earlier valid reactors and push such a trusted collaborator beyond the cap, so the workflow never calls `trust_of` for that approval and re-quarantines the issue. This is the same deterministic public-input denial identified in round 1 for the supported write-role approval path. Merely warning that the authoritative evidence was discarded does not preserve the promised durable approval, and the new self-test explicitly locks in the defective result (`zzz` is trusted but expected to be unprobed and rejected).
issues.fix_hint: Use a bounded source/order that cannot be selected by public reactors—for example, derive the eligible write+ identities authoritatively and intersect them with the reaction evidence before applying any bound. Alternatively, explicitly narrow the product contract and trust logic to only the exact-match identities instead of continuing to advertise and accept general write+ approvals. Add an executed crowd test with a non-exact-match write/maintain/admin reactor beyond 50 attacker-controlled logins and require that its approval is honored.
issues.title: Public reactors can still crowd out write-role approvals

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-two change prevents crowd-out only for the two exact-match identities. The advertised and implemented approval policy still accepts any write/maintain/admin collaborator, but those trusted reactors remain in the attacker-orderable capped population and can still be deterministically discarded. The prior major finding therefore remains materially unresolved.
